clue.text: Entire Boeotian city beginning to trust 12

definitions.note: 12-across is a toast, and this is another farewell or toast wishing someone well

parts.note: entire means all, the whole lot
Thebes was the chief city of Boeotia in ancient Greece

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here of trust

explanation.surface: A traveller's note on an ancient Greek city and the first hint of trust between people.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' sends you to 12-across, CHEERS, the theme word: every themed answer is a toast or a parting wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are said when raising a glass or bidding goodbye, wishing someone good fortune.

clue.text: Tuna and shaved bacon: real toasted sandwiches!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the other piece between them like bread round a filling
toasted suggests the letters of real are cooked up into a new arrangement
shaved means trimmed at the end, so bacon loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before the trim

explanation.surface: A café menu boasting a tuna option alongside proper toasted bacon sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toasted' rearranges REAL into AL...RE, which 'sandwiches' BACO, the word bacon 'shaved' of its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a species of tuna, the long-finned kind often canned as white meat.

clue.text: Valiants playing Igors Stepanovs and Marians Pahars?

definitions.note: two footballers from a Baltic country who played in England; the question mark shows they are examples

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the word are put into a different line-up

explanation.surface: A football team called the Valiants fielding two Baltic players in its side.
explanation.walkthrough: Igors Stepanovs (Arsenal) and Marians Pahars (Southampton) were footballers from Riga's country; Charlton Athletic's nickname is the Valiants, which helps the football picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The two players named are examples of nationals of the Baltic state whose capital is Riga.

clue.text: Strong liquor — a scream when given to small children!

indicators.note: one piece is handed to, so placed before, the other

parts.note: something or someone very funny is a hoot or a scream
CH is a short form of children, small signalling the shortening

explanation.surface: A joke that strong drink handed to little ones would be a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang for strong or illicit spirits, especially homemade or smuggled alcohol.

clue.text: Brahms and Liszt describe him, heartlessly, with dishonour

indicators.note: Brahms and Liszt is Cockney rhyming slang for drunk, which signals the letters reel into a new order
heartlessly means the middle letter of him is taken out, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Two Romantic composers writing a damning account of some man's disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms and Liszt' is rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk; the drunken letters are DESCRIBE plus HM, which is 'him, heartlessly' without its I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be smeared or sullied in reputation is to be marked with dishonour or disgrace.

clue.text: Fans rejecting brown bitter drinks …

indicators.note: rejecting means a piece is thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: fans of a team are its supporters
porter is a dark brown beer, bitter in taste

explanation.surface: Supporters turning down a dark ale and choosing other drinks instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this clue to 6-down for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to take liquid in small mouthfuls, so sups means sips or drinks.

clue.text: Drink in the bar regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Ordering a drink in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is a common hot drink brewed from leaves.

clue.text: … soak a measure of whisky up and sway

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to ret flax is to soak it to soften the fibres
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A drunk downing whisky and starting to wobble on his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' looks like a drunkard, but here it is the verb RET; 'up' turns RET plus TOT over.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to move unsteadily, rocking or swaying as if about to fall.

clue.text: Mocking one with no worries

parts.note: one is the article a
to tease is to mock playfully; a tease is a mocking one

explanation.surface: Someone who teases others while staying carefree themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Mocking one' as a tease, A plus TEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relaxed and free from anxiety is the idiomatic state of being comfortable.

clue.text: Made one's point in keeping up success

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece holds the other up, so it sits above it

parts.note: a hit is a success, as of a song or show
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone striking an argument home while staying on top of success.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'in' (HOME) 'keeping up' HIT means HIT is placed above HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that strikes home has its intended impact, so the speaker's argument has landed.

clue.text: 12 might be pub's motto

definitions.note: 12-across is a toast, and this is a jolly drinking toast urging glasses emptied

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A toast that a pub could take as its slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' points to CHEERS, the theme toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are cries when raising a glass, this one urging everyone to drink up.

clue.text: See 14
Two mates not finishing 12

definitions.note: 12-across is a toast, and this is an old-fashioned toast

indicators.note: two signals the trimmed word appears twice in a row
not finishing means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: Two friends who never quite finish their toast.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA, from 'china plate', is Cockney rhyming slang for a mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dated English toast, borrowed from a Chinese greeting, said when clinking glasses.

clue.text: A TV series brings comfort

definitions.meaning: an American sitcom set in a Boston bar
to raise someone's spirits or console them

explanation.surface: A sitcom that cheers people up.
explanation.walkthrough: The sitcom set in a Boston bar suits the drinking theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boston bar sitcom of the 1980s bears the name, and the verb means gladdens or comforts.

clue.text: Chap tucking into healthy meal on rotating hot plate

indicators.note: tucking into means one piece is placed inside the other, with a pun on eating

parts.note: a salad is a light, healthy meal
a chap is a man

indicators.note: rotating means the letters are turned round

parts.note: on means about, which is re

explanation.surface: A man digging into a salad served on a revolving hotplate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' reads as eating but is the container signal; the 'hot plate' is a chef's grill, not a plate of hot food.
explanation.definitionFit: In cookery this is an overhead grill or heated iron plate used for browning food.

clue.text: Mark timely change to hen

parts.note: put a ..., O, ..., which is THE plus N for ..., and you get these words

explanation.surface: A bird keeper noting the moment a cockerel is replaced by a hen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: put a ring (O) in 'the N', N being new, and you get T-O-HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To celebrate the arrival of a new year is to mark the timely change of calendar.

clue.text: Michael's getting drunk and dropping e for 12

definitions.note: 12-across is a toast, and this is the Hebrew toast meaning to life

indicators.note: getting drunk means the letters stagger into a new order
dropping means one letter is left out of the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: A man named Michael, now tipsy, slurring his vowels as he toasts.
explanation.walkthrough: MICHAEL less one E is shuffled into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Jewish toast, Hebrew for 'to life', said when glasses are raised.

clue.text: Killed alien over 12

definitions.note: 12-across is a toast, and this is the Gaelic toast meaning health

parts.note: killed means slain

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A tabloid shocker: alien slain, followed by a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Irish and Scottish Gaelic drinking toast, literally meaning health.

clue.text: Barrels arranged in a line for not especially regular event

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for barrel or barrels

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Barrels lined up for some occasional event.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair: an event every two years is regular, but not especially frequent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening once every two years recurs at intervals, but only occasionally.

clue.text: It perhaps runs one out of estuary

definitions.note: It is short for Italian, as in gin and It, an example of a fortified wine

indicators.note: out of means the pieces are taken away from the longer phrase

parts.note: an estuary is where a river meets the sea, its river mouth
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something flowing out of an estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is not a pronoun but Italian, the fortified wine of 'gin and It'; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is one kind of the aromatised fortified wine, the sweet red style.

clue.text: Play a song that's number one backwards

indicators.note: that's, read as that has, means the song holds the next piece

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

indicators.note: backwards means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: number one is a childish word for a wee

explanation.surface: A DJ playing a chart-topping song in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like the verb, but it is the noun meaning room to move; 'number one' is not a hit but a wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Play in a rope or a schedule is slack, the room or margin for movement.

clue.text: Straight down the hatch, as you'd expect with slammer?

definitions.text: down the hatch, as you'd expect with slammer?
definitions.meaning: a tequila slammer is downed in one gulp, the way you knock back a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Drinking a tequila slammer in one go, as tradition demands.
explanation.walkthrough: A tequila slammer is mixed with a fizzy drink, banged on the bar and downed at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly, and literally describes how a shot glass is drained.

clue.text: Run quickly curtailed when sustaining a joint injury

indicators.note: sustaining means holding up, so one piece carries the other inside it
curtailed means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to sprint is to run at full speed

explanation.surface: A runner who cuts a dash short after hurting a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted ankle or wrist with stretched ligaments is a common hurt to a joint.

clue.text: Second part of present old mum's wrapped for absentee …

indicators.note: wrapped means one piece is enclosed by the other, like a gift

parts.note: the present is the here and now, whose second part is now
mum's the word means keep quiet, so mum is sh

explanation.surface: Part of a present that an elderly mother has wrapped for someone who stayed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' is not a gift here but 'here and now'; this clue uses its second half and 23-down its first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fails to turn up for a booking or appointment is an absentee.

clue.text: … first part of present given to lady, not getting wrapping to stick

indicators.note: given to means one piece is placed alongside the other
without wrapping means the outer letters of lady are removed

parts.note: the present is the here and now, whose first part is here

explanation.surface: Half of a present handed to a lady, unwrapped, with something to stick it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' again means 'here and now', as in 22-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or be fixed firmly to a surface is the verb's literal sense.

clue.text: 12 offering resistance in advance

definitions.note: 12-across is a toast, and this is the Latin toast meaning may it benefit

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to posit is to put forward or advance an idea
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A toast that meets opposition before it is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a German and Latin drinking toast, literally 'may it do good'.

clue.text: A tincture making old driver mostly insensible

parts.note: Niki Lauda was a retired Formula One racing champion

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: insensible means numb, without feeling

explanation.surface: A tincture leaving a former racing driver almost senseless.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudanum is an alcoholic solution of opium, a tincture once used as a painkiller.

clue.text: Chillified offering for starters under cover of tortilla?

definitions.text: Chillified offering for starters under cover of tortilla?

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means one piece is placed below the other
the cover of a word is its outside letters, first and last
for starters means the opening letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: A spicy Mexican snack in a tortilla shell.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it, a chilli filling inside a tortilla.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a folded tortilla holding a spicy filling, a typical Mexican offering.

clue.text: See 20
Endure air played by noted New Year's Day performer

indicators.note: played means the letters are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: Sitting through a tune performed by a famous musician on New Year's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch violinist and conductor is famous for his waltz concerts, often broadcast at New Year.

clue.text: See 14
GP's concern is 12

definitions.meaning: a family doctor looks after a patient's wellbeing
12-across is a toast, and this toast wishes the drinkers well

explanation.surface: A doctor's concern for a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor cares about a patient's wellbeing, and the phrase is also a toast wishing good health.
